newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cedel Bank opposes existing debt redenomination.
newsitem.headline: Cedel Bank opposes existing debt redenomination.

text.p: Luxembourg-based Cedel Bank, supplier of clearing, settlement and custodial services, said on Wednesday it was opposing redenomination in Euros for existing debt securities in the run-up to European Monetary Union (EMU).
"Existing debt securities should not be redenominated," Cedel said in a statement outlining its plans to support EMU.

Noting that redenomination is an issuer's decision, it said that before it was opted for, careful consideration should be given to the associated cost, benchmark issues, the impact on liquidity for investors and the legal basis for redenomination.
But if it was found to be absolutely necessary, the legal basis for redenomination had to be undisputed both from an issuer's and investor's point of view, it said.
It said that the issuer should take all the necessary measures to dispel doubts about the legality of redenomination.
"National legislation should facilitate the redenomination process to the greatest extent possible," it said.

It said that, despite the announced 1:1 Ecu/Euro conversion rate, legal uncertainty could still exist for investors and issuers on conversion of debt securities issued prior to the Maastricht Treaty and under non-EU law.
"The competent European authorities should therefore seek discussions with the governments of non-EU countries with the aim of finding solutions avoiding potential litigation.

But among market intermediaries, transactions in non-redenominated debt securities should be settled in Euro, and payments of coupons and redemption proceeds should equally be made in Euro from the start of the transition period to EMU.
It said investors had to retain the right to choose the currency they wanted to pay or be paid in for as long as the national currencies remained legal tender.
Equally, issuers retain the right to choose the currency they want to pay in for as long as national currencies remain legal tender.
Cedel noted a lot of work had to be done before the start of the three-year EMU transition period on January 1, 1999.
"In systems terms, this is a very short time and many changes have to be made, each requiring planning, design, implementation and testing," it said.

Cedel, the only international depository operating links with all European Union countries, said its settlement turnover for 1996 exceeded $13 trillion. It holds $1.2 trillion of customers' securities in safekeeping.
